discovery.search

The search service identifies a matching set of documents which satisfy the caller's criteria, sorts it, and selects a subset of the matches to return as the result set. Each step can be controlled via parameters.

Available as lseg.data.discovery.search.

search(
    query: str | None = None,
    view: Views | str = Views.SEARCH_ALL,
    filter: str | None = None,
    order_by: str | None = None,
    boost: str | None = None,
    select: str | None = None,
    top: int = 10,
    skip: int = 0,
    group_by: str | None = None,
    group_count: int = 3,
    features: str | None = None,
    scope: str | None = None,
    terms: str | None = None,
    navigators: str | None = None,
    extended_params: ExtendedParams = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame

Parameters

Parameter Type Required Default Description
query str | None No None Keyword argument for view
view Views | str No Views.SEARCH_ALL The view for searching see at Views enum. Default: Views.SEARCH_ALL
filter str | None No None Where query is for unstructured end-user-oriented restriction, filter is for structured programmatic restriction.
order_by str | None No None Defines the order in which matching documents should be returned.
boost str | None No None This argument supports exactly the same predicate expression syntax as filter, but where filter restricts which documents are matched at all, boost just applies a large scoring boost to documents it matches, which will almost always guarantee that they appear at the top of the results.
select str | None No None A comma-separated list of the properties of a document to be returned in the response.
top int No 10 the maximum number of documents to retrieve. Must be non-negative. default: 10
skip int No 0 The number of documents to skip in the sorted result set before returning the next top.
group_by str | None No None If specified, this must name a single Groupable property. returned documents are grouped into buckets based on their value for this property.
group_count int No 3 When supplied in combination with group_by, sets the maximum number of documents to be returned per bucket. default: 3
features str | None No None Comma-separated list of flags, typically niche or experimental things which most callers won't want
scope str | None No None Name of a Symbol property against which Terms will be matched Example: "RIC"
terms str | None No None Comma-separated list of up to 5000 symbols to be matched against the Scope property Example": "A,B,C,D"
navigators str | None No None This can name one or more properties, separated by commas, each of which must be Navigable. Example: "HullType"
extended_params ExtendedParams No None Other parameters can be provided if necessary

Returns

pd.DataFrame

Example

import lseg.data as ld
df1 = ld.discovery.search(query="cfo", view=ld.discovery.Views.PEOPLE)
# What's the general distribution of earnings per share in the 0-20 range using fixed-value-width bucket ranges?
df2 = ld.discovery.search(
    view=ld.discovery.Views.EQUITY_QUOTES,
    top=0,
    filter="Eps gt 0 and Eps lt 20",
    navigators="Eps(type:histogram,buckets:4)"
)
# Top ten currencies for govcorp bonds, ranked by total outstanding value, along with the maximum coupon of each.
df3 = ld.discovery.search(
    view=ld.discovery.Views.GOV_CORP_INSTRUMENTS,
    top=0,
    navigators="Currency(buckets:10,desc:sum_FaceOutstandingUSD,calc:max_CouponRate)"
)
